SMTO-EXE-0098 — SMTO lost contact with the computer it was looking at

GUID: 7ad3f16d-9051-5b20-8362-dcce20056fb7
Slug: screen-gateway-lost
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • SMTO sent a screen request to the Gateway but didn't get a usable answer back. No screenshot was confirmed, and SMTO won't repeat the request on its own.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the computer running the Gateway is switched on, awake and connected to the network. SMTO can only reach the Gateway while that computer is online.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for that Gateway. This confirms SMTO can reach the same Gateway again and refreshes what it can do.
  3. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check for updates, and if an Update to button with a version number appears for that Gateway, use it while no task is running there. An older Gateway may not understand SMTO's screen requests and rejects them. Updating stops that Gateway's running tasks, so wait until they finish.
  4. Once it shows as connected, ask SMTO for the screenshot again in the chat. Looking at the screen changes nothing, so a new request is safe once the Gateway is back.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway shows as connected and SMTO returns the screenshot.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't ask SMTO to capture a different computer's screen instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected Gateway returned no usable screen result: the screen route raised an HTTP or outbound-connection error (400/404/405/422/501 are treated as rejected), a connection failure occurred, or cancellation could not be confirmed.

What this means

  • The screen route received an HTTP or transport error, failed request processing or could not confirm cancellation, leaving no usable observation receipt. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • The screen route received an HTTP or transport error, failed request processing or could not confirm cancellation, leaving no usable observation receipt.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original request phase and retained artifact information before restoring the same verified Gateway route.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the original request and any published artifact in the run first. Reconnect the same Gateway and refresh its capabilities (a 404/405/501 usually means the Gateway predates the /screen/operation route, so update it), then issue a new explicit observation; GatewayClient never retries screen capture automatically.
  • Restore the selected route and inspect the original request/artifact status. Make another capture only as a new explicit observation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Reconnect the same selected Gateway and refresh its capabilities. No observation success is established and capture is not automatically repeated. Any already published artifact follows normal run cleanup.

How to verify the fix

  • The original request is settled and any separately requested observation returns its own valid result.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
